# croccante

Minimal nginx-rtmp relay container. Receives one RTMP program stream on port
1935 and, only after an authenticated Start command, relays it without
transcoding to any number of destinations.

```
                                   ┌─► rtmp://…   (supervisor 1 ─ ffmpeg -c copy)
Alana ─► [host:1935] ─► nginx-rtmp ├─► rtmps://…  (supervisor 2 ─ ffmpeg -c copy)
                                   └─► rtmp://…   (supervisor 3 ─ ffmpeg -c copy)
```

Each destination gets its own long-lived supervisor process that retries
forever with backoff, so one dead or rejecting destination never affects the
others, and a network blip resolves itself without restarting anything.

## Configuring destinations

Croccante accepts no destination URLs or stream keys in environment variables.
At authenticated Start, Alana supplies an exact configuration version plus one
to twenty opaque IDs and versioned AWS Secrets Manager references:

```json
{
  "version": "destinations-2026-08-25.1",
  "destinations": [
    {"id": "primary", "secretId": "broadcast/example/primary", "versionId": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"}
  ]
}
```

Each referenced secret is a strict JSON object containing only `scheme`,
`host`, optional `port`, `application`, and `streamKey`. Croccante resolves
every exact version before opening any output and binds the resulting selection
immutably to that session. A secret rotation takes effect only through an
explicit Stop, validation/reload, and new Start.

## Explicit broadcast lifecycle

One Croccante runtime serves one required `PROGRAM_ID`. Its control API listens
on port 8081 and must stay on the private `broadcast-control` Docker network.
It requires a bearer token mounted at `CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE`; the token is never
accepted on the command line or returned by the API.

An RTMP publisher may connect while Croccante is stopped, but public
destinations remain disconnected until Alana sends an authenticated Start.
Start and Stop require both an `Idempotency-Key` and a monotonically increasing
`X-Command-Sequence`. Stop ends every public output without restarting the
container. Publisher loss during a started session invokes filler and never
implies Stop.

Before Start, Alana prepares an immutable program-scoped filler version through
the same authenticated private API. Croccante downloads the signed source,
verifies its checksum, transcodes it once to the supplied H.264/AAC live profile,
and stores it on the durable filler volume. Start names the prepared version with
`X-Filler-Version`; unprepared or mismatched versions are refused, and an active
session never switches versions.

The machine contract and example requests are documented in
[docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md#lifecycle-control-api).

The versioned, credential-free contract for future as-aired recording manifests
and bounded operator reports is documented in
[docs/recording-contract.md](docs/recording-contract.md). This defines the
fixture-backed boundary only; runtime capture and production wiring remain in
[issue #17](https://github.com/gaulatti/croccante/issues/17).

The same private listener exposes authenticated Prometheus metrics at
`GET /metrics`. It reports container process, publisher, relay, retry,
backoff, filler, and control-request behavior using bounded labels only. The
endpoint never emits program names, destination URLs, stream keys, or
credentials. See [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md#prometheus-metrics).

RTMPS is handled natively by ffmpeg. Resolved URLs are injected at its I/O
boundary from root-only runtime state, so keys never appear in process
arguments. See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Publisher settings

| Field      | Value                          |
|------------|--------------------------------|
| Service    | Custom                         |
| Server     | `rtmp://<server-ip>:1935/live` |
| Stream key | anything (e.g. `stream`)       |

## Running it

Server setup, deployment, and key rotation live in
[docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md).

Locally:

```bash
docker build -t croccante:dev .
docker run --rm -p 1935:1935 \
  -e PROGRAM_ID=example-program \
  -e AWS_REGION=us-east-1 \
  --mount type=bind,src="$PWD/control-token",dst=/run/secrets/croccante-control-token,readonly \
  --mount type=bind,src="$PWD/aws-credentials",dst=/run/secrets/aws-credentials,readonly \
  -e AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/run/secrets/aws-credentials \
  croccante:dev
```

## Tests

```bash
python3 -m pip install coverage==7.17.0
python3 -m coverage run --branch --source=. --omit='test/*' -m unittest discover -s test -p 'test_*.py'
python3 -m coverage report -m
./test/smoke.sh
```

The unit suite needs `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` and Python 3.12 or newer. It runs every
Python module in this repository: real local ffmpeg preparation for image,
silent video and WebM-with-audio fillers; the authenticated lifecycle, filler
and destination routes and the Start/Stop state machine of `control-server.py`
served over real HTTP in-process (supervisors are tiny shell scripts, secrets
come from the explicit non-production file provider, and subprocess, signal,
clock and filesystem faults are injected, so no Docker, nginx-rtmp or ffmpeg
relay is needed); destination parsing, AWS and file secret providers; the
metrics collector's `/proc` sources; and the recording manifest rejection matrix,
artifact verification and bounded redacted reports. The smoke harness brings up
local RTMP and RTMPS sinks, runs the relay, and asserts on actual relayed bytes
plus authenticated lifecycle and metrics behavior. It needs Docker, touches no
real platform account and no real stream key, and also runs in CI on every push.

On macOS with Colima, set `TMPDIR` to an existing directory shared with that
VM (for example a private directory under your home folder); the smoke harness
honors it for its temporary fake-secret bind mounts. macOS `mktemp` without a
template can otherwise select an unshared `/var/folders` path, which Docker
mounts as a directory rather than the expected secret file. The harness removes
its fake-secret files and disposable containers on exit.

## Pull request verification

Local agent review uses the shared `clouseau` skill and `.clouseau-local.json`;
it needs no CI provider keys. Every PR runs the unit suite with **exactly 100%
line and branch coverage** over all application Python (measured by
coverage.py with branch measurement and no exclusion patterns or pragmas, then
validated by Clouseau's complete source inventory), the Clouseau and workflow
security tests, and the real relay smoke harness. After those pass, Clouseau
reviews the change against [.github/clouseau.md](.github/clouseau.md), approves
and arms auto-merge. See [docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md](docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md).

Merging and deploying are separate. `deploy.yml` runs on `main` pushes only when
a file that ships in the image changes (see `deployment.paths` in
`.github/clouseau.json`); Clouseau merges use a token that does not start push
workflows, so it dispatches the deployment explicitly in that case. Deploying
replaces the live relay and interrupts a broadcast for a few seconds.

## File map

```
croccante/
├── Dockerfile           # Alpine + nginx-mod-rtmp + ffmpeg
├── nginx.conf           # RTMP ingest + loopback stat endpoint (static, not templated)
├── destination_store.py # Strict selection parsing and exact secret resolution
├── destination_runtime.py # Atomic supervisor ownership for one session
├── destination_url_shim.c # Keeps resolved output URLs out of ffmpeg argv
├── entrypoint.sh        # Initializes stopped state and execs nginx
├── relay-dest.sh        # One supervisor per destination: relay, retry, back off
├── relay-start.sh       # nginx exec_publish hook   — records the live stream name
├── relay-stop.sh        # nginx exec_publish_done   — clears it
├── relay-lib.sh         # Shared helpers (atomic writes, pid checks, counters)
├── healthcheck.sh       # Relay-aware container healthcheck
├── control-server.py    # Authenticated, program-scoped Start/Stop/state API
├── relay_metrics.py     # Bounded Prometheus collector for private scraping
├── recording_manifest.py # Versioned recording manifest validation and reports
├── contracts/           # Closed machine-readable recording contract schemas
├── filler_store.py      # Durable immutable source preparation and validation
├── docs/                # Architecture and operations (destined for the wiki)
├── test/smoke.sh        # End-to-end harness against local sinks
└── .github/workflows/deploy.yml
```

# Croccante review contract

Croccante is a single-program RTMP relay appliance: one container combines
nginx-rtmp ingest, per-destination ffmpeg supervisors, a private authenticated
lifecycle and metrics API, and a durable immutable filler store. Alana publishes
one program stream to it; Croccante alone resolves versioned destination secrets
from AWS Secrets Manager and fans the stream out without transcoding.

Preserve the private `broadcast-control` boundary, authenticated Start/Stop with
idempotency keys and increasing sequences, immutable per-session destination and
filler bindings, per-destination failure isolation, publisher-gap filler, and
secret redaction. Stream keys and full destination URLs never appear in APIs,
logs, metrics, process arguments or durable evidence. A command being accepted is
not proof of delivery; supervisor state and real output bytes establish that
result. Startup never invents a prior operator Start.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance can serve this existing appliance without a new product
decision. Protocol correctness, recovery, redaction, bounded metrics and
documented runbooks are established obligations. New capabilities must have
repository documentation or linked acceptance criteria that establish their
actual need and boundaries. The as-aired recording and delivery-report capability
is tracked separately in the repository's issues and is not implied by the
existing manifest contract.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example turning the relay into a general streaming platform, exposing the
control API publicly, moving stream keys out of Secrets Manager, or changing the
Alcantara to Alana to Croccante control chain. Ordinary implementation
uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated investigation, not routine
human code review. Changes to review controls, coverage exclusions, or this
purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions,
test-only readiness paths and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed.
Subprocess, signal, socket, clock and filesystem fault injection is legitimate
when the real application contract and failure handling remain exercised. The
real relay smoke harness must separately prove nginx-rtmp ingest, ffmpeg
supervision, filler engagement, destination isolation and parsed bounded metrics.

All tests and exactly 100% application line and branch coverage remain mandatory
for every contribution, including external forks, with no coverage-ignore
directives. Unloaded modules must be measured. Missing or unresolved integrity
evidence holds approval; intent confirmation cannot waive it. Contributor code
never receives provider, repair or approval credentials, and fork PRs cannot
trigger automatic repairs.

Clouseau owns the shared scoring, investigation, repair bounds, evidence ledger,
native approval and auto-merge. This repository owns its purpose, real tests and
runtime evidence. CI/merge, image deployment and live relay health are separate
milestones: merging changes that do not alter the shipped image never deploys.
A production deployment interrupts a live broadcast, so every file that ships in
the image is a protected path: a change to one needs the owner's explicit intent
confirmation before it can merge. A successful merge alone is not a deployment
or delivery claim.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine content,
expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. This route has no AI credentials and
must not fall back to paid review when verification fails. All native tests,
exact coverage, relay smoke checks and branch protections remain mandatory.
Agent installation and account-authenticated local execution remain independent
of CI enrollment and CI provider keys. A signature authenticates the workstation;
it does not attest against compromise of that workstation or its operator.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Opt-in as-aired capture of Croccante's final relay/filler output.

This module is the recorder runtime for the v1 recording contract
(`recording_manifest.py`). It is deliberately separate from Alana's clean
program master: it records what Croccante actually put on the air, including
filler intervals and gaps, plus a redacted delivery report.

Isolation is the central rule. `AsAiredCapture` never raises into its caller:
any recorder or report failure is counted, the session is closed as `failed`
or `partial`, and the relay keeps running. Nothing here reads, stores, or
emits a destination URL or stream key; the only URL handed to the recorder is
the local source to capture, and it is used only as an ffmpeg argument.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Mapping
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from recording_manifest import (
    CLASSIFICATIONS,
    CONTRACT_VERSION,
    DESTINATION_ATTEMPT_STATUSES,
    ERROR_CODES,
    MAX_ATTEMPTS,
    MAX_DESTINATIONS,
    MAX_ERRORS,
    MAX_SEGMENTS,
    MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS,
    MAX_TRANSITIONS,
    SOURCE_MODES,
    load_manifest,
    render_session_report,
    validate_manifest,
)

MIN_SEGMENT_SECONDS = 2
MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS = 60
MAX_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
MAX_QUOTA_BYTES = 1_099_511_627_776
CONTAINER = "mpegts"
EXTENSION = "ts"
_TERMINAL = frozenset({"complete", "partial", "failed"})
_LOOPBACK = frozenset({"127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"})
# Evidence headroom kept free so a saturated session can still close validly.
_RESERVE = 4


class CaptureConfigError(ValueError):
    """The opt-in capture settings are missing, ambiguous, or out of bounds."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CaptureSettings:
    """Explicit opt-in settings. There is no default-enabled instance."""

    root: Path
    source: str
    segment_seconds: int
    max_session_bytes: int
    max_total_bytes: int
    retention_days: int
    classification: str
    video: dict[str, Any] | None
    audio: dict[str, Any] | None
    legal_hold: bool = False

    @staticmethod
    def from_mapping(raw: Mapping[str, Any] | None, *, root: Path) -> "CaptureSettings | None":
        """Return None unless capture was explicitly enabled; reject bad values."""

        if raw is None or raw.get("enabled") is not True:
            return None
        allowed = {
            "enabled", "source", "segmentSeconds", "maxSessionBytes", "maxTotalBytes",
            "retentionDays", "classification", "legalHold", "video", "audio",
        }
        if set(raw) - allowed:
            raise CaptureConfigError("unknown_setting")

        def integer(name: str, low: int, high: int) -> int:
            value = raw.get(name)
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or not low <= value <= high:
                raise CaptureConfigError(f"invalid_{name}")
            return value

        source = raw.get("source")
        if not isinstance(source, str) or not _local_source(source):
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_source")
        classification = raw.get("classification")
        if not isinstance(classification, str) or classification not in CLASSIFICATIONS:
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_classification")
        video, audio = raw.get("video"), raw.get("audio")
        if not all(item is None or isinstance(item, dict) for item in (video, audio)) or (video is None and audio is None):
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_profile")
        legal_hold = raw.get("legalHold", False)
        if not isinstance(legal_hold, bool):
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_legalHold")
        settings = CaptureSettings(
            root=root,
            source=source,
            segment_seconds=integer("segmentSeconds", MIN_SEGMENT_SECONDS, MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS),
            max_session_bytes=integer("maxSessionBytes", 1, MAX_QUOTA_BYTES),
            max_total_bytes=integer("maxTotalBytes", 1, MAX_QUOTA_BYTES),
            retention_days=integer("retentionDays", 1, MAX_RETENTION_DAYS),
            classification=classification,
            video=video,
            audio=audio,
            legal_hold=legal_hold,
        )
        if settings.max_session_bytes > settings.max_total_bytes:
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_maxSessionBytes")
        return settings


def _local_source(source: str) -> bool:
    """An absolute local path, or a credential-free loopback rtmp:// URL."""

    if source.startswith("/"):
        return "://" not in source
    parts = urlsplit(source)
    return parts.scheme == "rtmp" and parts.hostname in _LOOPBACK and parts.username is None and parts.password is None


def build_capture_command(settings: CaptureSettings, session_dir: Path, start_number: int) -> list[str]:
    """ffmpeg arguments for the capture leg: stream copy into numbered segments."""

    return [
        "ffmpeg", "-nostdin", "-loglevel", "error", "-i", settings.source,
        "-map", "0", "-c", "copy", "-f", "segment",
        "-segment_time", str(settings.segment_seconds),
        "-segment_format", CONTAINER, "-segment_start_number", str(start_number),
        "-reset_timestamps", "1",
        str(session_dir / "artifacts" / f"segment-%06d.{EXTENSION}"),
    ]


def build_probe_command(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    return [
        "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-print_format", "json",
        "-show_entries", "stream=codec_type,codec_name,width,height,avg_frame_rate,sample_rate,channels:format=duration",
        str(path),
    ]


def parse_probe(output: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Reduce ffprobe JSON to the contract's bounded media facts."""

    document = json.loads(output)
    duration_ms = round(float(document["format"]["duration"]) * 1000)
    video = audio = None
    for stream in document["streams"]:
        if stream["codec_type"] == "video" and video is None:
            numerator, denominator = (int(part) for part in stream["avg_frame_rate"].split("/"))
            video = {
                "codec": stream["codec_name"], "width": stream["width"], "height": stream["height"],
                "frameRate": {"numerator": numerator, "denominator": denominator},
            }
        elif stream["codec_type"] == "audio" and audio is None:
            audio = {"codec": stream["codec_name"], "sampleRateHz": int(stream["sample_rate"]), "channels": stream["channels"]}
    return {"durationMs": duration_ms, "video": video, "audio": audio}


def default_probe(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    result = subprocess.run(build_probe_command(path), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, check=True)
    return parse_probe(result.stdout)


def default_start(command: list[str]) -> subprocess.Popen:
    return subprocess.Popen(command, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def _iso(moment: datetime) -> str:
    moment = moment.astimezone(timezone.utc)
    return moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.") + f"{moment.microsecond // 1000:03d}Z"


def _sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as source:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    temporary = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")
    temporary.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    os.replace(temporary, path)


def derive_source_timeline(
    noted: list[tuple[int, str]], segments: list[dict[str, Any]], elapsed_ms: int
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Source timeline that agrees with the captured segments.

    A noted `live`/`filler` mode only applies while a segment covers the time;
    uncovered time (before the first segment, between segments, or after the
    last) is `unobserved`, which is how gaps stay visible.
    """

    if elapsed_ms == 0:
        return []
    covered = [(s["startedOffsetMs"], s["startedOffsetMs"] + s["durationMs"]) for s in segments]
    points = {0, elapsed_ms, *(offset for offset, _ in noted if offset < elapsed_ms)}
    for start, end in covered:
        points.update((start, end))
    ordered = sorted(point for point in points if point <= elapsed_ms)
    timeline: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for start, end in zip(ordered, ordered[1:]):
        in_segment = any(low <= start and end <= high for low, high in covered)
        mode = "unobserved"
        if in_segment:
            for offset, noted_mode in noted:
                if offset <= start:
                    mode = noted_mode
        if not timeline or timeline[-1]["mode"] != mode:
            timeline.append({"sequence": len(timeline) + 1, "startedOffsetMs": start, "mode": mode})
    return timeline


class AsAiredSession:
    """One recording session; builds only manifests the v1 validator accepts."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: CaptureSettings,
        *,
        destination_count: int,
        configuration_hash: str,
        clock: Callable[[], datetime],
        session_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if not 1 <= destination_count <= MAX_DESTINATIONS:
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_destination_count")
        self.settings = settings
        self.session_id = session_id or str(uuid.uuid4())
        self.directory = settings.root / self.session_id
        self._clock = clock
        self._configuration_hash = configuration_hash
        self._opened = self._now()
        self._transitions: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"sequence": 1, "state": "pending", "at": _iso(self._opened), "reasonCode": None}]
        self._state = "pending"
        self._recording_started: datetime | None = None
        self._segments: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self._noted: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
        self._destinations: list[list[dict[str, Any]]] = [[] for _ in range(destination_count)]
        self._errors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self._final: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        self._profile: dict[str, Any] = {"container": CONTAINER, "video": settings.video, "audio": settings.audio, "timeBase": "milliseconds"}
        self._next_offset = 0
        self._elapsed_base = 0
        self._elapsed_at_close = 0
        self._interrupted_at: datetime | None = None
        self._gap_ms = 0
        self._interruptions = 0
        self.truncated: str | None = None
        self._cursor = 1
        (self.directory / "artifacts").mkdir(parents=True)
        self.persist()

    # -- clock and offsets -------------------------------------------------
    def _now(self) -> datetime:
        moment = self._clock().astimezone(timezone.utc)
        return moment.replace(microsecond=moment.microsecond // 1000 * 1000)

    def _offset_ms(self) -> int:
        if self._recording_started is None:
            return 0
        return max(self._elapsed_base, self._elapsed_base + int((self._now() - self._recording_started).total_seconds() * 1000))

    def _move(self, state: str, reason: str | None = None) -> None:
        self._transitions.append({"sequence": len(self._transitions) + 1, "state": state, "at": _iso(self._now()), "reasonCode": reason})
        self._state = state

    @property
    def state(self) -> str:
        return self._state

    @property
    def terminal(self) -> bool:
        return self._state in _TERMINAL

    @property
    def segment_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self._segments)

    @property
    def next_file_number(self) -> int:
        """Number of the next capture file to read (ffmpeg numbering, which can skip)."""

        return self._cursor

    @property
    def saturated(self) -> bool:
        """True when contract evidence bounds leave no room for more history."""

        return (
            len(self._errors) >= MAX_ERRORS - _RESERVE
            or len(self._transitions) >= MAX_TRANSITIONS - _RESERVE
            or any(len(attempts) >= MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1 for attempts in self._destinations)
            or len(self._noted) >= MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS - _RESERVE
            or len(derive_source_timeline(self._noted, self._segments, max(self._offset_ms(), self._next_offset))) >= MAX_SOURCE_EVENTS - _RESERVE
        )

    def saturate(self) -> None:
        """Stop recording more history: the rest of the broadcast is unobserved."""

        self.truncated = self.truncated or "capture_interrupted"
        if not any(error["code"] == "capture_interrupted" for error in self._errors):
            self.record_error("capture", "capture_interrupted", False)

    @property
    def total_bytes(self) -> int:
        return sum(segment["byteLength"] for segment in self._segments)

    # -- recorded facts ----------------------------------------------------
    def record_error(self, phase: str, code: str, retryable: bool) -> None:
        self._errors.append({"sequence": len(self._errors) + 1, "at": _iso(self._now()), "phase": phase, "code": code, "retryable": retryable})

    def start_recording(self) -> None:
        self._move("recording")
        self._recording_started = self._now()
        self._noted.append((0, "live"))  # the relay is live until a filler transition is noted

    def note_source(self, mode: str) -> None:
        """Record a relay/filler transition at the current session offset."""

        if mode not in SOURCE_MODES - {"unobserved"}:
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_source_mode")
        offset = self._offset_ms()
        if self._noted and self._noted[-1][0] == offset:
            self._noted[-1] = (offset, mode)
        else:
            self._noted.append((offset, mode))

    def begin_destination_attempt(self, slot: int) -> None:
        attempts = self._attempts(slot)
        if attempts and attempts[-1]["status"] == "in_progress":
            raise CaptureConfigError("attempt_already_in_progress")
        attempts.append({"sequence": len(attempts) + 1, "startedAt": _iso(self._now()), "endedAt": None, "status": "in_progress", "observedBytes": 0, "errorCode": None})

    def end_destination_attempt(self, slot: int, status: str, observed_bytes: int, error_code: str | None) -> None:
        """Close the open attempt. Evidence the v1 contract would reject is refused
        before it can enter session state."""

        attempts = self._attempts(slot)
        code = None if status == "accepted" else error_code or "destination_unavailable"
        if (
            not attempts or attempts[-1]["status"] != "in_progress"
            or status not in DESTINATION_ATTEMPT_STATUSES - {"in_progress"}
            or isinstance(observed_bytes, bool) or not isinstance(observed_bytes, int) or observed_bytes < 0
            or (status == "accepted" and observed_bytes == 0)
            or (code is not None and code not in ERROR_CODES)
        ):
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_destination_evidence")
        attempts[-1].update(endedAt=_iso(self._now()), status=status, observedBytes=observed_bytes, errorCode=code)
        if code is not None:
            self.record_error("delivery", code, status == "failed")

    def _attempts(self, slot: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        if isinstance(slot, bool) or not isinstance(slot, int) or not 1 <= slot <= len(self._destinations):
            raise CaptureConfigError("invalid_slot")
        return self._destinations[slot - 1]

    def add_segment(self, path: Path, probe: Callable[[Path], dict[str, Any]]) -> bool:
        """Consume one finished capture file.

        Returns True when the file was handled and capture may continue: either
        registered, or (when it cannot be probed) discarded as a visible gap.
        Returns False, after discarding the file, when the per-session quota is
        reached or the measured codecs differ from the declared profile; the
        session then stops growing and ends `partial`.
        """

        self._cursor += 1
        size = path.stat().st_size
        if self.total_bytes + size > self.settings.max_session_bytes or len(self._segments) >= MAX_SEGMENTS:
            path.unlink()
            self.truncated = "disk_full"
            self.record_error("storage", "disk_full", False)
            return False
        try:
            facts = probe(path)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - an unverifiable segment is a gap, not a reason to stop recording
            path.unlink()
            self._interruptions += 1
            self._next_offset += self.settings.segment_seconds * 1000
            self.record_error("capture", "capture_interrupted", True)
            return True
        if facts["video"] != self._profile["video"] or facts["audio"] != self._profile["audio"]:
            path.unlink()
            self.truncated = "capture_interrupted"
            self.record_error("capture", "capture_interrupted", False)
            return False
        sequence = len(self._segments) + 1
        target = path.with_name(f"segment-{sequence:06d}.{EXTENSION}")
        if target != path:
            os.replace(path, target)
        self._segments.append({
            "kind": "segment", "sequence": sequence, "storageKey": f"artifacts/{target.name}",
            "startedOffsetMs": self._next_offset, "durationMs": facts["durationMs"], "byteLength": size, "sha256": _sha256(target),
        })
        self._next_offset += facts["durationMs"]
        return True

    def interrupt(self, code: str) -> None:
        self._interrupted_at = self._now()
        self._interruptions += 1
        self.record_error("capture", code, True)
        self._move("interrupted", code)

    def resume(self, code: str) -> None:
        """interrupted -> recovering -> recording; the gap stays `unobserved`."""

        self._move("recovering", code)
        self._move("recording")
        now = self._now()
        missed = int((now - self._interrupted_at).total_seconds() * 1000)
        self._gap_ms += missed
        self._next_offset += missed
        self._elapsed_base = self._next_offset
        self._recording_started = now

    # -- manifest ----------------------------------------------------------
    def _retention(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        anchor = datetime.strptime(self._transitions[-1]["at"], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ") if self.terminal else self._opened
        delete_after = None if self.settings.legal_hold else _iso(anchor.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=self.settings.retention_days))
        return {"classification": self.settings.classification, "deleteAfter": delete_after, "legalHold": self.settings.legal_hold}

    def manifest(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        elapsed = self._elapsed_at_close if self.terminal else max(self._offset_ms(), self._next_offset)
        destinations = []
        for index, attempts in enumerate(self._destinations, 1):
            if not attempts:
                final = "not_attempted" if self.terminal else "pending"
            else:
                final = "pending" if attempts[-1]["status"] == "in_progress" else attempts[-1]["status"]
            destinations.append({"slot": index, "finalStatus": final, "attempts": [dict(item) for item in attempts]})
        return {
            "contractVersion": CONTRACT_VERSION,
            "sessionId": self.session_id,
            "configurationHash": self._configuration_hash,
            "state": self._state,
            "openedAt": _iso(self._opened),
            "closedAt": self._transitions[-1]["at"] if self.terminal else None,
            "transitions": [dict(item) for item in self._transitions],
            "capture": {
                "profile": {**self._profile},
                "elapsedDurationMs": elapsed,
                "capturedDurationMs": sum(segment["durationMs"] for segment in self._segments),
                "droppedFrames": 0,
                "sourceTimeline": derive_source_timeline(self._noted, self._segments, elapsed),
                "segments": [dict(segment) for segment in self._segments],
                "finalArtifact": self._final,
            },
            "destinations": destinations,
            "errors": [dict(error) for error in self._errors],
            "retention": self._retention(),
        }

    def persist(self) -> None:
        """Validate before writing so an invalid state is never published."""

        manifest = self.manifest()
        validate_manifest(manifest)
        _atomic_write(self.directory / "manifest.json", json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
        if self.terminal:
            _atomic_write(self.directory / "report.txt", render_session_report(manifest))

    # -- close -------------------------------------------------------------
    def fail(self, code: str, phase: str) -> None:
        """Terminate with `failed` (no final artifact is allowed)."""

        self._elapsed_at_close = self._next_offset
        self.record_error(phase, code, False)
        self._move("failed", code)
        self._final = None
        self._close_open_attempts()
        self.persist()

    def _close_open_attempts(self) -> None:
        """Unresolved attempts become `unknown`, recorded once to stay within bounds."""

        closed = False
        for attempts in self._destinations:
            if attempts and attempts[-1]["status"] == "in_progress":
                attempts[-1].update(endedAt=_iso(self._now()), status="unknown", errorCode="finalization_failed")
                closed = True
        if closed:
            self.record_error("delivery", "finalization_failed", False)

    def finalize(self) -> None:
        """Concatenate verified segments into one artifact, then close the session."""

        self._elapsed_at_close = self._next_offset
        self._move("finalizing")
        self._close_open_attempts()
        problem: str | None = None
        if self._interruptions or not self._segments:
            problem = "capture_interrupted"
            if not any(error["code"] == problem for error in self._errors):
                self.record_error("capture", problem, False)
        else:
            try:
                self._final = self._concatenate()
            except OSError:
                problem = "finalization_failed"
                self.record_error("finalization", problem, False)
        failed_delivery = any(attempts and attempts[-1]["status"] != "accepted" for attempts in self._destinations)
        undelivered = any(not attempts for attempts in self._destinations)
        reason = problem or self.truncated or ("destination_unavailable" if failed_delivery or undelivered else None)
        if reason is None:
            self._move("complete")
        else:
            if not any(error["code"] == reason for error in self._errors):
                self.record_error("delivery", reason, False)  # only delivery reasons are not already recorded
            self._move("partial", reason)
        self.persist()

    def _concatenate(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        target = self.directory / "artifacts" / f"final.{EXTENSION}"
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        with target.open("wb") as output:
            for segment in self._segments:
                with (self.directory / segment["storageKey"]).open("rb") as source:
                    for chunk in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                        digest.update(chunk)
                        output.write(chunk)
        size = target.stat().st_size
        if size != self.total_bytes or digest.hexdigest() != _sha256(target):
            raise OSError("final artifact verification failed")
        return {"kind": "final", "storageKey": f"artifacts/final.{EXTENSION}", "durationMs": self._elapsed_at_close, "byteLength": size, "sha256": digest.hexdigest()}


class AsAiredCapture:
    """Failure-isolated facade used by the relay. No method ever raises."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: CaptureSettings,
        *,
        destination_count: int,
        configuration_hash: str,
        clock: Callable[[], datetime] = lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        start: Callable[[list[str]], Any] = default_start,
        probe: Callable[[Path], dict[str, Any]] = default_probe,
        session_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.settings = settings
        self.failures = 0
        self.session: AsAiredSession | None = None
        self._start, self._probe, self._process = start, probe, None
        self._stopped = False
        self._clock = clock
        self._args = (destination_count, configuration_hash, session_id)
        self._guard(self._open)

    def _guard(self, action: Callable[[], None]) -> bool:
        try:
            action()
            return True
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - the recorder must never disturb the relay
            self.failures += 1
            return False

    def _open(self) -> None:
        count, configuration_hash, session_id = self._args
        # A retention fault must not prevent the session; the quota check below still applies.
        self._guard(lambda: apply_retention(self.settings.root, self._clock(), self.settings.max_total_bytes))
        self.session = AsAiredSession(self.settings, destination_count=count, configuration_hash=configuration_hash, clock=self._clock, session_id=session_id)
        if usage(self.settings.root) > self.settings.max_total_bytes:
            self.session.fail("disk_full", "storage")
            return
        self.session.start_recording()
        self._launch()
        self.session.persist()

    def _launch(self) -> None:
        assert self.session is not None
        command = build_capture_command(self.settings, self.session.directory, self.session.next_file_number)
        self._process = self._start(command)

    def _alive(self) -> bool:
        return self._process is not None and self._process.poll() is None

    def _active(self) -> bool:
        return self.session is not None and not self.session.terminal

    def _record(self, action: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
        """Run a guarded mutation, then close the session if evidence bounds are reached."""

        if self._active() and self._guard(action) and self.session.saturated:
            self.session.saturate()
            self.close()

    def note_source(self, mode: str) -> None:
        """Called on every relay <-> filler transition."""

        self._record(lambda: self.session.note_source(mode))

    def destination_started(self, slot: int) -> None:
        self._record(lambda: self.session.begin_destination_attempt(slot))

    def destination_ended(self, slot: int, status: str, observed_bytes: int, error_code: str | None) -> None:
        self._record(lambda: self.session.end_destination_attempt(slot, status, observed_bytes, error_code))

    def poll(self) -> None:
        """Register finished segments, detect a crashed recorder, publish the manifest."""

        self._record(self._poll)

    def _poll(self) -> None:
        session = self.session
        assert session is not None
        directory = session.directory / "artifacts"
        while True:
            number = session.next_file_number
            current = directory / f"segment-{number:06d}.{EXTENSION}"
            following = directory / f"segment-{number + 1:06d}.{EXTENSION}"
            if not current.exists() or not (following.exists() or not self._alive()):
                break
            if not session.add_segment(current, self._probe):
                self._stop_process()
                break
            if session.saturated:
                break
        if not self._alive() and not self._stopped and session.state == "recording":
            session.interrupt("process_crashed")
            self._process = None
        session.persist()

    def recover(self) -> None:
        """Restart the capture process after a crash; the outage stays a visible gap."""

        if self._active() and self.session.state == "interrupted":
            def action() -> None:
                self.session.resume("process_crashed")
                self._launch()
            self._record(action)

    def _stop_process(self) -> None:
        self._stopped = True
        if self._process is not None and self._alive():
            self._process.terminate()
            self._process.wait(timeout=10)

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Stop capture and finalize. Failure leaves a failed/partial manifest, never an exception."""

        if not self._active():
            return
        if not self._guard(self._close):
            self._guard(lambda: self.session.fail("finalization_failed", "finalization"))

    def _close(self) -> None:
        assert self.session is not None
        self._stop_process()
        self._poll_after_stop()
        self.session.finalize()

    def _poll_after_stop(self) -> None:
        session = self.session
        assert session is not None
        directory = session.directory / "artifacts"
        while True:
            current = directory / f"segment-{session.next_file_number:06d}.{EXTENSION}"
            if not current.exists() or not session.add_segment(current, self._probe) or session.saturated:
                break

    def snapshot(self) -> dict[str, int | str]:
        """Bounded observability: counts and a closed state vocabulary only."""

        session = self.session
        return {
            "state": session.state if session else "unavailable",
            "segments": session.segment_count if session else 0,
            "bytes": session.total_bytes if session else 0,
            "recorder_failures": self.failures,
        }


def usage(root: Path) -> int:
    """Bytes held by capture sessions under `root`."""

    total = 0
    for path in root.glob("*/artifacts/*"):
        total += path.stat().st_size
    return total


def apply_retention(root: Path, now: datetime, max_total_bytes: int) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Delete expired terminal sessions, then oldest terminal sessions over quota.

    Only directories named by a v4 UUID that hold a valid terminal manifest are
    eligible; legal holds and non-terminal or unreadable sessions are never
    deleted.
    """

    result = {"expired": 0, "quota": 0, "kept": 0}
    if not root.is_dir():
        return result
    candidates = []
    for directory in sorted(root.iterdir()):
        try:
            uuid.UUID(directory.name, version=4)
            manifest = load_manifest(directory / "manifest.json")
        except (ValueError, OSError):
            continue
        if manifest["state"] not in _TERMINAL or manifest["retention"]["legalHold"]:
            continue
        candidates.append((manifest["closedAt"], directory, manifest["retention"]["deleteAfter"]))
    current = _iso(now)
    remaining = []
    for closed_at, directory, delete_after in sorted(candidates):
        if delete_after <= current:
            shutil.rmtree(directory)
            result["expired"] += 1
        else:
            remaining.append(directory)
    for directory in remaining:
        if usage(root) <= max_total_bytes:
            break
        shutil.rmtree(directory)
        result["quota"] += 1
    result["kept"] = sum(1 for _ in root.iterdir())
    return result

# Recording manifest and session report contract

Croccante owns the evidence of what it captured and attempted to deliver. The
v1 contract is intentionally independent of a recorder process, media
container, storage provider, and destination transport so the runtime work in
[#17](https://github.com/gaulatti/croccante/issues/17) can consume it without
inventing another lifecycle or persistence format.

The machine-readable shape is
[`contracts/recording-session-v1.schema.json`](../contracts/recording-session-v1.schema.json).
`recording_manifest.py` enforces the schema's structural rules plus the ordered
state, timing, checksum, finalization, retry, and privacy rules that JSON Schema
cannot express by itself. Producers and consumers must call
`validate_manifest`; validating against the JSON Schema alone is insufficient.

## Ownership boundary

| Concern | Owner | Recorded by this contract |
|---------|-------|---------------------------|
| Program intent, scheduling, operator authorization, Start/Stop | Alana | No. Alana keeps the program-to-session mapping outside this artifact. |
| As-aired bytes observed at Croccante, segment order, gaps, final artifact | Croccante | Yes: slot-neutral media facts and SHA-256 checksums. |
| Attempted delivery to configured outputs | Croccante | Yes: numbered slots, attempts, final status, and closed error codes. |
| Platform-side playback, archive acceptance, or audience receipt | Destination/platform | No. `accepted` means the transport accepted Croccante's attempt and bytes were observed; it is not a claim about downstream playback. |
| Artifact upload/storage wiring and retention execution | #17 runtime | No runtime is introduced here; v1 defines the evidence that implementation must write and enforce. |

The manifest deliberately has no program ID, operator ID, destination ID,
hostname, URL, stream key, token, signed request, free-form note, or raw error.
`sessionId` must be a generated RFC 4122 version-4 UUID, not a user or program
identifier. This is a producer and privacy invariant: UUID shape alone cannot
prove that a producer did not improperly reuse a UUID-shaped user identifier.
`configurationHash` is the SHA-256 of the already-redacted,
immutable destination selection; destination results use contiguous slots only.

## Version and compatibility

Every document declares exactly
`croccante.recording-session/v1`. All objects are closed: an unknown or missing
field is invalid. Consumers must reject an unknown contract version rather than
guessing. JSON decoders must also reject duplicate keys at every nesting level;
first-key/last-key ambiguity is not a valid interpretation. Any field addition,
semantic change, new state, or new error code
therefore requires a new version and a documented migration. V1 readers remain
valid for the lifetime of retained v1 manifests.

Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339 values ending in `Z`. Durations and offsets are
integer milliseconds. Checksums are lowercase SHA-256 hex. Media container and
codec names are bounded identifiers, not runtime commands or URLs. Artifact
keys are relative `artifacts/segment-NNNNNN.ext` or `artifacts/final.ext`
references. The storage root remains an implementation choice.

## State and finalization

Every manifest starts with transition 1 in `pending`. Transition sequence
numbers are contiguous, timestamps never move backwards, and the top-level
`state` equals the last transition.

| From | Allowed next state |
|------|--------------------|
| `pending` | `recording`, `failed` |
| `recording` | `interrupted`, `finalizing`, `failed` |
| `interrupted` | `recovering`, `finalizing`, `failed` |
| `recovering` | `recording`, `finalizing`, `failed` |
| `finalizing` | `complete`, `partial`, `failed` |

`complete`, `partial`, and `failed` are terminal. An interrupted recorder makes
recovery explicit (`interrupted → recovering → recording`) rather than silently
rewriting history. Interrupted, recovering, partial, and failed transitions
carry a closed `reasonCode`; ordinary progress states do not. A `complete`
session requires verified segments, a final artifact whose duration equals the
elapsed session duration, and successful final status for every
destination. A `partial` or `failed` session requires at least one structured
error. Failed sessions cannot claim a final artifact.

A pending snapshot has no capture progress, source events, dropped frames,
destination attempts, or errors. Nonterminal snapshots cannot claim a final
artifact, and terminal snapshots cannot leave destination status pending. These
state gates prevent a structurally valid object from describing an impossible
lifecycle combination.

Segment numbers are contiguous from one. Offsets are monotonic and cannot
overlap. `capturedDurationMs` equals the sum of segment durations, while
`elapsedDurationMs` reaches at least the end of the last segment and may be
larger when an interruption created a gap. This distinction preserves a crash
without pretending missing media was captured.

When present, the final artifact preserves the elapsed session timeline: its
duration equals `elapsedDurationMs`, including any explicitly unobserved gap.
The finalizer must represent that gap with neutral media rather than collapsing
time. Consequently every source-timeline and session-report offset maps directly
to the same final-artifact offset; `capturedDurationMs` remains the truthful sum
of bytes captured in segments.

`sourceTimeline` begins at offset zero and records up to 64 `live`, `filler`, or
`unobserved` intervals. Adjacent events cannot repeat a mode. Its observed
intervals must match the exact union of segment intervals; an unobserved
interval therefore cannot be disguised as captured media. Reports aggregate
each mode in milliseconds and render every `offset:mode` event, preserving
relay/filler visibility and artifact-relative timecode linkage without including
publisher or program identifiers. The profile records
container plus structured video dimensions/frame rate and audio rate/channels;
an audio-only or video-only fixture is valid, but at least one stream is
required.

## Delivery, errors, and retry evidence

Destination slots are contiguous from one and contain up to 32 ordered
attempts. Before the first attempt, an active session uses `finalStatus: pending`;
a terminal preflight failure uses `not_attempted` and an empty attempt
list. An active `in_progress` attempt has a null end time and makes the final
status pending. Finished attempts are `accepted`, `failed`, or `unknown`.
Accepted means a transport accepted the attempt and Croccante observed a
positive byte count; it does not mean a platform played or archived the media.
Failed and unknown attempts require a closed error code. A destination's final
status must match its last finished attempt. Retries append attempts; they never
replace prior evidence. This preserves separate attempted, in-flight, accepted,
failed, unknown, and not-attempted facts.

Errors contain only sequence, timestamp, phase, closed code, and whether the
condition was retryable. They have no arbitrary message field. V1 codes cover
capture interruption, process crash, disk/storage failure, checksum failure,
finalization failure, and destination failure. Diagnostic logs may hold richer
private detail under their own access and retention rules, but that detail must
not enter the manifest or report.

Error sequences are contiguous and timestamps are monotonic. An error tied to
an interrupted/failed transition or a failed/unknown destination attempt cannot
predate the event that made it observable. Repeated same-code failures are
matched occurrence-by-occurrence to ordered error records, so a later retry
cannot borrow an earlier failure's evidence.

## Retention and privacy

The manifest records one classification (`public-broadcast`, `internal`, or
`restricted`) and either a future `deleteAfter` timestamp or `legalHold: true`.
A legal hold forbids a deletion timestamp. This is an instruction and audit
fact; #17 must make deletion enforcement atomic with artifact ownership and
must preserve the manifest long enough to prove the result. Moving media to a
new storage provider must not change its checksum or silently extend retention.
For a terminal session, `deleteAfter` must be later than `closedAt`, not merely
later than when the session opened.

Before persistence, `validate_manifest(..., artifact_root=...)` checks every
declared file's byte length and SHA-256. Structural validation also rejects
credential-, URL-, raw-error-, and user-identity-bearing field names at any
depth. Runtime implementations must validate before making a manifest durable
and again before publishing a session report.

## Session report

`render_session_report` returns exactly nine newline-terminated lines and at
most 4,096 UTF-8 bytes. It contains only the generated session UUID, lifecycle
state/timing, aggregate capture and live/filler/unobserved timecode facts,
final-artifact presence, aggregate attempted/in-flight/accepted/failed/unknown
destination evidence and observed bytes, closed error-code counts, and
retention facts. It never renders storage keys, configuration hashes,
destination identifiers, URLs,
credentials, user identifiers, or raw errors. Error counts are sorted, so the
same valid manifest always produces identical bytes.

## Contract fixtures

`test/fixtures/recording` includes complete, partial, crashed-and-recovered,
disk-full, destination-failure, active-in-flight, and preflight-failure
manifests. The focused test creates tiny, deterministic, license-free PCM WAV
payloads in a temporary directory, verifies
their declared byte lengths and checksums, and removes them on completion. No
recording media or generated output is committed. Negative tests cover invalid
transitions, missing checksums, sequence/duration inconsistencies, modified
artifact bytes, unsafe fields, and identity-bearing values.

This change does not start capture, write production artifacts, upload media,
alter delivery, or add runtime metrics. #17 remains the sole production-wiring
boundary; when it implements these state transitions, runtime counters should
use only the same closed state/error values and destination slots.

prove that a producer did not improperly reuse a UUID-shaped user identifier.
`configurationHash` is the SHA-256 of the already-redacted,
immutable destination selection; destination results use contiguous slots only.

## Version and compatibility

Every document declares exactly
`croccante.recording-session/v1`. All objects are closed: an unknown or missing
field is invalid. Consumers must reject an unknown contract version rather than
guessing. JSON decoders must also reject duplicate keys at every nesting level;
first-key/last-key ambiguity is not a valid interpretation. Any field addition,
semantic change, new state, or new error code
therefore requires a new version and a documented migration. V1 readers remain
valid for the lifetime of retained v1 manifests.

Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339 values ending in `Z`. Durations and offsets are
integer milliseconds. Checksums are lowercase SHA-256 hex. Media container and
codec names are bounded identifiers, not runtime commands or URLs. Artifact
keys are relative `artifacts/segment-NNNNNN.ext` or `artifacts/final.ext`
references. The storage root remains an implementation choice.

## State and finalization

Every manifest starts with transition 1 in `pending`. Transition sequence
numbers are contiguous, timestamps never move backwards, and the top-level
`state` equals the last transition.

| From | Allowed next state |
|------|--------------------|
| `pending` | `recording`, `failed` |
| `recording` | `interrupted`, `finalizing`, `failed` |
| `interrupted` | `recovering`, `finalizing`, `failed` |
| `recovering` | `recording`, `finalizing`, `failed` |
| `finalizing` | `complete`, `partial`, `failed` |

`complete`, `partial`, and `failed` are terminal. An interrupted recorder makes
recovery explicit (`interrupted → recovering → recording`) rather than silently
rewriting history. Interrupted, recovering, partial, and failed transitions
carry a closed `reasonCode`; ordinary progress states do not. A `complete`
session requires verified segments, a final artifact whose duration equals the
elapsed session duration, and successful final status for every
destination. A `partial` or `failed` session requires at least one structured
error. Failed sessions cannot claim a final artifact.

A pending snapshot has no capture progress, source events, dropped frames,
destination attempts, or errors. Nonterminal snapshots cannot claim a final
artifact, and terminal snapshots cannot leave destination status pending. These
state gates prevent a structurally valid object from describing an impossible
lifecycle combination.

Segment numbers are contiguous from one. Offsets are monotonic and cannot
overlap. `capturedDurationMs` equals the sum of segment durations, while
`elapsedDurationMs` reaches at least the end of the last segment and may be
larger when an interruption created a gap. This distinction preserves a crash
without pretending missing media was captured.

When present, the final artifact preserves the elapsed session timeline: its
duration equals `elapsedDurationMs`, including any explicitly unobserved gap.
The finalizer must represent that gap with neutral media rather than collapsing
time. Consequently every source-timeline and session-report offset maps directly
to the same final-artifact offset; `capturedDurationMs` remains the truthful sum
of bytes captured in segments.

`sourceTimeline` begins at offset zero and records up to 64 `live`, `filler`, or
`unobserved` intervals. Adjacent events cannot repeat a mode. Its observed
intervals must match the exact union of segment intervals; an unobserved
interval therefore cannot be disguised as captured media. Reports aggregate
each mode in milliseconds and render every `offset:mode` event, preserving
relay/filler visibility and artifact-relative timecode linkage without including
publisher or program identifiers. The profile records
container plus structured video dimensions/frame rate and audio rate/channels;
an audio-only or video-only fixture is valid, but at least one stream is
required.

## Delivery, errors, and retry evidence

Destination slots are contiguous from one and contain up to 32 ordered
attempts. Before the first attempt, an active session uses `finalStatus: pending`;
a terminal preflight failure uses `not_attempted` and an empty attempt
list. An active `in_progress` attempt has a null end time and makes the final
status pending. Finished attempts are `accepted`, `failed`, or `unknown`.
Accepted means a transport accepted the attempt and Croccante observed a
positive byte count; it does not mean a platform played or archived the media.
Failed and unknown attempts require a closed error code. A destination's final
status must match its last finished attempt. Retries append attempts; they never
replace prior evidence. This preserves separate attempted, in-flight, accepted,
failed, unknown, and not-attempted facts.

Errors contain only sequence, timestamp, phase, closed code, and whether the
condition was retryable. They have no arbitrary message field. V1 codes cover
capture interruption, process crash, disk/storage failure, checksum failure,
finalization failure, and destination failure. Diagnostic logs may hold richer
private detail under their own access and retention rules, but that detail must
not enter the manifest or report.

Error sequences are contiguous and timestamps are monotonic. An error tied to
an interrupted/failed transition or a failed/unknown destination attempt cannot
predate the event that made it observable. Repeated same-code failures are
matched occurrence-by-occurrence to ordered error records, so a later retry
cannot borrow an earlier failure's evidence.

## Retention and privacy

The manifest records one classification (`public-broadcast`, `internal`, or
`restricted`) and either a future `deleteAfter` timestamp or `legalHold: true`.
A legal hold forbids a deletion timestamp. This is an instruction and audit
fact; #17 must make deletion enforcement atomic with artifact ownership and
must preserve the manifest long enough to prove the result. Moving media to a
new storage provider must not change its checksum or silently extend retention.
For a terminal session, `deleteAfter` must be later than `closedAt`, not merely
later than when the session opened.

Before persistence, `validate_manifest(..., artifact_root=...)` checks every
declared file's byte length and SHA-256. Structural validation also rejects
credential-, URL-, raw-error-, and user-identity-bearing field names at any
depth. Runtime implementations must validate before making a manifest durable
and again before publishing a session report.

## Session report

`render_session_report` returns exactly nine newline-terminated lines and at
most 4,096 UTF-8 bytes. It contains only the generated session UUID, lifecycle
state/timing, aggregate capture and live/filler/unobserved timecode facts,
final-artifact presence, aggregate attempted/in-flight/accepted/failed/unknown
destination evidence and observed bytes, closed error-code counts, and
retention facts. It never renders storage keys, configuration hashes,
destination identifiers, URLs,
credentials, user identifiers, or raw errors. Error counts are sorted, so the
same valid manifest always produces identical bytes.

## Contract fixtures

`test/fixtures/recording` includes complete, partial, crashed-and-recovered,
disk-full, destination-failure, active-in-flight, and preflight-failure
manifests. The focused test creates tiny, deterministic, license-free PCM WAV
payloads in a temporary directory, verifies
their declared byte lengths and checksums, and removes them on completion. No
recording media or generated output is committed. Negative tests cover invalid
transitions, missing checksums, sequence/duration inconsistencies, modified
artifact bytes, unsafe fields, and identity-bearing values.

This change does not start capture, write production artifacts, upload media,
alter delivery, or add runtime metrics. #17 remains the sole production-wiring
boundary; when it implements these state transitions, runtime counters should
use only the same closed state/error values and destination slots.

## As-aired capture runtime (`as_aired_capture.py`)

The module is opt-in and dark: nothing in the shipped image imports it or copies
it yet, and `CaptureSettings.from_mapping` returns `None` unless `enabled` is
exactly `true`. It records Croccante's final relay/filler output as a separate
as-aired artifact; it never reads, writes, or replaces Alana's clean program
master.

- **Capture leg.** `build_capture_command` is `ffmpeg -c copy` into numbered
  MPEG-TS segments under `<root>/<sessionId>/artifacts/`. The source must be an absolute local path or a credential-free `rtmp://`
  URL whose host is exactly `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1`, never a destination. A segment is
  registered only after the next segment exists (or the process ended), so a
  half-written segment is never verified.
- **Verification.** Each registered segment gets a SHA-256, byte length and an
  ffprobe duration, and its video/audio codecs must equal the declared profile.
  A mismatch discards the segment and closes the session `partial`. A segment
  that cannot be probed is discarded as a visible `unobserved` gap (the session
  can then only end `partial`) and later segments are renamed so artifact keys
  stay contiguous. Finalization
  concatenates the verified segments to `artifacts/final.ts`, re-hashes it, and
  compares its size to the sum of the segments.
- **Transitions and delivery.** `note_source("live"|"filler")` records relay and
  filler intervals (live until the first filler is noted); time not covered by a
  segment is `unobserved`. `begin_destination_attempt` / `end_destination_attempt`
  record numbered slots with `accepted`, `failed`, `unknown` or in-progress
  states. The slot number is the only destination identity written.
- **Crash tolerance.** If the capture process dies, the session becomes
  `interrupted` with `process_crashed`; `recover` restarts numbering where it
  left off and the outage stays an `unobserved` gap. A session with a gap, no
  segments, a failed final artifact, a quota stop, a codec change, or a failed or
  unattempted destination ends `partial`, never `complete`. Failed sessions never
  carry a final artifact.
- **Evidence bounds.** The v1 caps (64 errors, transitions and source events,
  32 attempts per slot) are never exceeded: when a session approaches one it
  stops recording history and closes `partial` with `capture_interrupted`, so a
  long broadcast with a flapping destination or publisher still ends with a
  valid terminal manifest and report.
- **Failure isolation.** `AsAiredCapture` never raises: every relay callback is
  guarded, failures are counted (`snapshot()["recorder_failures"]`), a close that
  cannot finalize writes a `failed` manifest, and an invalid manifest is never
  written (the previous valid one stays). The report is
  `render_session_report` of the validated manifest, written next to it.
- **Quota and retention.** `maxSessionBytes` stops capture at the first segment
  that would exceed it (`disk_full`); `maxTotalBytes` is checked before a session
  records (a full store yields a `failed` preflight manifest). Opening a session
  first runs `apply_retention`, which deletes expired terminal sessions and then
  the oldest terminal sessions over the total quota. Legal holds, non-terminal
  sessions and directories that are not valid sessions are never deleted.
- **Observability.** `snapshot()` is the bounded surface (state, segment count,
  bytes, failure count). Prometheus exposition belongs to the wiring work in
  `relay_metrics.py`.

Offsets of relay/filler transitions come from the host clock and the segment
timeline from ffprobe durations, so a transition is accurate to the clock skew
between them, not to a frame.

Unverified here: a live relay soak, the Start/Stop wiring, image packaging, and
real-time capture from a running relay. The ffmpeg command and the ffprobe
parser were exercised against a synthetic MPEG-TS source during development.

class Clock:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.now = START

    def __call__(self) -> datetime:
        return self.now

    def advance(self, **delta: int) -> None:
        self.now += timedelta(**delta)


class FakeProcess:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.alive = True
        self.terminated = False

    def poll(self):
        return None if self.alive else 1

    def terminate(self) -> None:
        self.terminated = True
        self.alive = False

    def wait(self, timeout: int) -> None:
        self.waited = timeout

        "maxSessionBytes": 10_000, "maxTotalBytes": 20_000, "retentionDays": 7,

class Base(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.clock = Clock()
        self.settings = CaptureSettings.from_mapping(raw(), root=self.root)
        self.processes: list[FakeProcess] = []

    def start(self, command):
        self.commands = getattr(self, "commands", []) + [command]
        process = FakeProcess()
        self.processes.append(process)
        return process

    def facade(self, **kwargs) -> AsAiredCapture:
        args = {"destination_count": 2, "configuration_hash": HASH, "clock": self.clock, "start": self.start, "probe": probe}
        args.update(kwargs)
        return AsAiredCapture(self.settings, **args)

    def segment(self, session_dir: Path, number: int, size: int = 100) -> Path:
        path = session_dir / "artifacts" / f"segment-{number:06d}.ts"
        path.write_bytes(bytes([number]) * size)
        self.clock.advance(seconds=10)  # a 10 s segment takes 10 s of wall time to air
        return path

    def manifest(self, cap: AsAiredCapture) -> dict:
        return json.loads((cap.session.directory / "manifest.json").read_text())

+The module is opt-in and dark: nothing in the shipped image imports it or copies

+  MPEG-TS segments under `<root>/<sessionId>/artifacts/`. The source must be an absolute local path or a credential-free `rtmp://`

"""Opt-in as-aired capture of Croccante's final relay/filler output.

This module is the recorder runtime for the v1 recording contract
(`recording_manifest.py`). It is deliberately separate from Alana's clean
program master: it records what Croccante actually put on the air, including
filler intervals and gaps, plus a redacted delivery report.

Isolation is the central rule. `AsAiredCapture` never raises into its caller:
any recorder or report failure is counted, the session is closed as `failed`
or `partial`, and the relay keeps running. Nothing here reads, stores, or
emits a destination URL or stream key; the only URL handed to the recorder is

# croccante

Minimal nginx-rtmp relay container. Receives one RTMP program stream on port
1935 and, only after an authenticated Start command, relays it without
transcoding to any number of destinations.

```
                                   ┌─► rtmp://…   (supervisor 1 ─ ffmpeg -c copy)
Alana ─► [host:1935] ─► nginx-rtmp ├─► rtmps://…  (supervisor 2 ─ ffmpeg -c copy)
                                   └─► rtmp://…   (supervisor 3 ─ ffmpeg -c copy)
```

Each destination gets its own long-lived supervisor process that retries
forever with backoff, so one dead or rejecting destination never affects the
others, and a network blip resolves itself without restarting anything.

## Configuring destinations

Croccante accepts no destination URLs or stream keys in environment variables.
At authenticated Start, Alana supplies an exact configuration version plus one
to twenty opaque IDs and versioned AWS Secrets Manager references:

```json
{
  "version": "destinations-2026-08-25.1",
  "destinations": [
    {"id": "primary", "secretId": "broadcast/example/primary", "versionId": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"}
  ]
}
```

Each referenced secret is a strict JSON object containing only `scheme`,
`host`, optional `port`, `application`, and `streamKey`. Croccante resolves
every exact version before opening any output and binds the resulting selection
immutably to that session. A secret rotation takes effect only through an
explicit Stop, validation/reload, and new Start.

# Croccante review contract

Croccante is a single-program RTMP relay appliance: one container combines
nginx-rtmp ingest, per-destination ffmpeg supervisors, a private authenticated
lifecycle and metrics API, and a durable immutable filler store. Alana publishes
one program stream to it; Croccante alone resolves versioned destination secrets
from AWS Secrets Manager and fans the stream out without transcoding.

Preserve the private `broadcast-control` boundary, authenticated Start/Stop with
idempotency keys and increasing sequences, immutable per-session destination and
filler bindings, per-destination failure isolation, publisher-gap filler, and
secret redaction. Stream keys and full destination URLs never appear in APIs,
logs, metrics, process arguments or durable evidence. A command being accepted is
not proof of delivery; supervisor state and real output bytes establish that
result. Startup never invents a prior operator Start.

operational maintenance can serve this existing appliance without a new product
decision. Protocol correctness, recovery, redaction, bounded metrics and
documented runbooks are established obligations. New capabilities must have
repository documentation or linked acceptance criteria that establish their
actual need and boundaries. The as-aired recording and delivery-report capability

existing manifest contract.
